title: Audit event completeness for Cycle-1 mutations
objective: Verify every delivered mutation path (login success/fail/logout, asset create, asset update) produces an AuditEvent with required fields: actor, actor_type, action, target, before/after, outcome, correlation_id, UTC timestamp.
preconditions: audit query access (pytest DB or admin API).
test_data: one of each mutation performed in earlier tests
steps: Perform: failed login, successful login, asset create, asset PATCH, logout.
Validate required field presence and types for each.
expected_result: 5 matching events found; every event has non-null actor (or anonymous identifier for failed login), action, created_at UTC, outcome, correlation_id; create has before=null/after=snapshot; update has both snapshots; no secrets (passwords, session IDs, CSRF tokens) in any payload.

title: Audit hash chain integrity fields present
objective: Verify audit rows carry prev_hash/record_hash forming a verifiable SHA-256 chain per design §10.1.
test_data: all audit rows ordered by created_at
steps: Fetch audit rows in insertion order.
Verify each record_hash is a 64-hex SHA-256 value.
Verify each row's prev_hash equals the previous row's record_hash (genesis row excepted).
If the hashing formula is documented, recompute one record_hash and compare.
expected_result: Chain links are consistent; recomputation (where formula documented) matches; any gap/mismatch is a defect.

title: Audit events are append-only via application paths
objective: Verify no application endpoint allows editing or deleting audit events; direct ORM/DB permission model revokes UPDATE/DELETE for the app role where implemented.
test_data: attempted PATCH/DELETE on any exposed audit endpoint; attempted ORM update in pytest (if DB-permission revocation implemented)
steps: Probe API surface for audit mutation endpoints (none should exist for Cycle 1).
If an audit read endpoint exists, attempt unsafe methods on it.
In pytest, attempt AuditEvent.objects.filter(...).update(...) and .delete() and observe behavior.
expected_result: No mutation endpoint exists (405/404); unsafe methods rejected; if DB-level revocation implemented, ORM update/delete raises permission error; at minimum, application code provides no edit/delete path and events remain immutable through the API.

title: Correlation ID propagation into audit events
objective: Verify a client-supplied X-Correlation-ID on a mutation is echoed in the response and stored on the resulting AuditEvent.
steps: POST /assets with the fixed correlation ID header.
Query the AuditEvent for this create.
expected_result: Response echoes the same correlation ID; AuditEvent.correlation_id equals it; when no header is supplied, a server-generated UUID is used consistently across response, logs, and audit.
